title: A thermistor divider for the ADC
story: A 10 kohm NTC thermistor (B = 3950) must measure 0 C to 50 C with a 3.3 V ADC. It is 33.6 kohm at 0 C and 3.59 kohm at 50 C. The same divider is drawn twice: on the left as it is on a cold day (0 C), on the right on a hot day (50 C). The thermistor sits on top; choose the fixed bottom resistor (the same value in both copies). The cold reading must stay above 0.5 V and the hot reading below 2.8 V, so neither end is squashed against the ADC's limits, and the hot reading must be at least 1.5 V above the cold one, so the range is well used.

goals.label: hot reading at least 1.5 V above cold reading

hints: The fixed resistor that gives the biggest swing between two thermistor values is the geometric mean: sqrt(33.6 k x 3.59 k).
Too small a fixed resistor keeps both readings near 0 V; too big a one pushes both near 3.3 V.
